It combines the Bulk Synchronous Parallel (BSP) model with the Parallel Disk Model (PDM) to account for local computation, local disk I/O, and inter-processor communication [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the BSP-Disk model combines the BSP parallel computation model and the PDM parallel disk model. It further confirms that algorithms designed for this model consider local computation (Tw), local disk I/O (Tio), and communication (Tc), which aligns perfectly with the claim.

The model was developed to bridge the gap between theoretical parallel computation models (BSP and PDM) and the practical constraints of PC clusters, specifically the limited bandwidth and high gap factor $g$ of inter-node communication [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the BSP-Disk model 'very closely describes the characteristics of a PC cluster' and combines the BSP and PDM models. Furthermore, it notes that 'In PC clusters, communication is the least scalable factor when data size becomes larger due to relatively low bandwidth and large gap factor g,' which supports the claim that the model addresses these specific practical constraints.
